FILENAME_IS_NOW_MISLEADING: this file is named MORE_ACCURATE_AND_STILL_FAILS and, against the reachable bar A26 established, the scope does NOT fail -- it passes at 0.7363x. The name is kept because commits and briefs cite it, and renaming would break those. The finding the file exists for is untouched and is what A26 was built from: our error here is 7.95x smaller than upstream's own and the two errors are anti-aligned at cos -0.273, so agreement is worse than accuracy would suggest. What changed is only which bar that is scored against.

controls_on_the_conditioning_scope.note: the break control moves 3.5x here, which is what a break control is supposed to do -- unlike the diffusion arm, where destroying the sample pairing LOWERED the headline because the port's own error already exceeded the perturbation. A saturated control is a property of how bad the arm is, not of the control.

headline: our diffusion_conditioning gradient is EIGHT TIMES MORE ACCURATE than the bf16 training step we are trying to reproduce -- 0.015328 from the float64 ideal against their 0.121864 -- and it still fails agreement with that step at 1.0414x, because the two errors are anti-aligned (cos -0.2727) and so add instead of nesting.

what: the campaign's bar, re-read after of3t-direct measured diffusion_conditioning against upstream's own training gradient. The bar 'no further from their gradient than they are from the ideal' is STRICTER than 'as accurate as they are', and on 36.9462 % of the model the difference decides the verdict.
why_this_is_a_protocol_matter_and_not_a_: the bar is correct for a TRAJECTORY claim: to argue our optimizer step lands where theirs lands, agreement with their step is what matters and error direction counts. It is the wrong bar for an ACCURACY claim, and this campaign's foundation is that parity means accuracy, not bit-exactness. A port strictly more accurate than the reference has not failed to reproduce it on accuracy grounds. PROTOCOL A25 now requires three numbers and the cosine for every comparison against a reference that is not the ideal, and requires a verdict to say which bar it is against.
